newsitem.title: USA: Arraignment for Ennis Cosby suspect postponed.
newsitem.headline: Arraignment for Ennis Cosby suspect postponed.

text.p: Arraignment for the man accused of killing entertainer Bill Cosby's son Ennis was postponed for two weeks Thursday when two of his lawyers said the suspected gunman could not afford their services.

Mikhail Markhasev's lawyers Charles Lindner and Dale Ruben were excused from the case by Superior Court Judge John Reid and replaced by two court-appointed attorneys, Henry Hall and Harriet Hawkings. Lindner and Ruben said Markhasev's family could no longer pay for their services.
Reid set the arraignment and the unsealing of the grand jury indictment against Markhasev for May 13.
News reports said Markhasev, an 18-year-old Ukrainian immigrant, was believed to have been with two friends who may have witnessed the shooting in the early morning of Jan. 16.

USA Today reported Thursday that in statements to police, Eli Zakaria, 23, and Sara Ann Peters, 21, both of Huntington Beach, south of Los Angeles, said they were driving around with Markhasev in Zakaria's car that night.

According to the statements, the three friends stopped at a phone 450 feet from the isolated spot where Cosby was changing a tire. While Zakaria was on the phone, allegedly trying to reach a drug dealer, Markhasev headed up the street toward Cosby, the statements reportedly said.
The paper said Zakaria was alleged to have said that Markhasev shot Cosby.
Lindner said the story came as a surprise to him. "I am curious as to how they obtained the documents they claim to have," he said. All records in the case have been sealed.

A man who said he was the 23-year-old Zakaria's uncle told Los Angeles television station KTTV his nephew said he and his girlfriend went to a park-and-ride area near fashionable Mulholland Drive and got "high" on drugs.

The uncle said the three parked about 120 yards from where Cosby was shot. He said his nephew told him he went to make a phone call and Markhasev walked away, saying he was going to do a carjacking. Markhasev returned to the car later and admitted the killing, the uncle said.
Cosby, 27, was killed with a single gunshot.
